sourceInformation.source: Super Breakout (Atari, 1981 Atari 2600 release; 1978 arcade original)
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 WebGPURenderer with WebGL2 fallback; Rapier 2D 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio; AI Hub Session Protocol v1 client 1.4.0; esbuild 0.28.2
sourceInformation.artDirection: Cel-shaded space arcade; chunky ink outlines, rainbow force fields, cream paper and dark teal grid
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and keyframe tracks for field telemetry and paddle squash; procedural ball trails and debris
sourceInformation.audio: Code-written Web Audio music (10% default), synthesized arcade effects and Animalese-style gibberish; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub shared-world host-authoritative 1–2 player co-op; same-browser BroadcastChannel rooms; manual WebRTC LAN/VPN links; couch co-op
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium WebGPU/WebGL, scripted physics campaign, gamepad emulation, touch profiles, offline audio analysis, two-page multiplayer and official AI Hub harness
sourceInformation.research: Atari Super Breakout instruction manual and scanned manual: variants, scoring, five serves, contact-angle aiming, acceleration, roof shrink, sparse rainbow visuals and eight scoring sound variations; official Three.js r180 source and AI Hub protocol

testingFeedback: Testing and test-led review caught 9 behavioral issues: captive self-clearing, autopilot lock, invisible paddle collisions, guest keyboard movement, linked encore restart, controller checkbox focus, stale final victory snapshots, a failed optional GPU recovery path, and controller scrolling of long credits. All were fixed or removed.
4 were considered game-breaking in an affected mode: captive self-clearing, invisible collisions, guest keyboard movement, and stale multiplayer victory snapshots.
The natural four-stage scripted campaign broke all 272 bricks, rescued both captive balls, used 26 beats and reached the real victory UI through normal stage transitions.
Syntax-only checks provided less gameplay confidence than collision, input, multiplayer and full-campaign tests.
engineFeedback: Three.js r180 provides native toon node materials and AnimationMixer alongside its WebGPU renderer; Rapier supplies reliable continuous ball collision detection.

Rapier collider disabling alone still produced an upper-paddle hit after kinematic updates; zero collision groups fixed it. Software WebGPU screenshots were blank, so visuals were checked through the renderer’s WebGL2 fallback.
The campaign rules, controller-first menus, synthesized audio, attract player and host-authoritative multiplayer lifecycle.
Keeping precise arcade paddle aiming and captive-ball rules consistent with physical collision events.
Provide clearer WebGPU device-loss and headless capture diagnostics; software captures can be blank despite a live simulation.
promptFeedback: The distinctive source, controller-first direction and complete-demo requirement made the target clear.
The source year names the Atari 2600 release while the original arcade game dates to 1978; the manual resolved the intended mechanics.
Making the same complete campaign and menus work across controllers, touch, standalone networking and AI Hub.
Specify a target campaign length and whether standalone online play requires Internet NAT traversal or LAN support.

aiHub.name: Super Breakbeat
aiHub.tagline: Return the signal. Break the silence.
aiHub.description: A cel-shaded interstellar brick breaker with four signal fields, stacked paddles, captive multiballs and an advancing final wall. Charge a rescue beat and fly solo or share the signal in two-player co-op.
aiHub.controls: Left stick / A D / arrows / mouse / touch: move; Cross / A / Space / click: serve; Square / X / Shift / right click / two fingers: beat; Options / Escape: menu.
